text.p: UnionAmerica Holdings Plc said Friday it expects improvement in cash flow and operating net in 1998.

"The initiatives we have developed to succeed in a difficult market environment are now producing clear top-line premium growth in 1997. It is our strong expectation that this will translate into clear improvements in both cash flows and operating earnings in 1998," said Chairman and Chief Executive Philip Marcell.

"To the extent that the dollar remains at the current level with the (British) pound, we will see an exchange translation benefit within operating overheads during the remaining nine months of 1997 to offset this charge. We do anticipate the quarterly operating earnings number growing in 1997 to achieve our expected post-tax return on average 1997 shareholders' equity for the full year in excess of 15 percent," he said.

The company reported first quarter operating income, excluding realized capital losses, of $4.1 million or $0.47 per fully diluted share, This compares with operating income of $4.6 million, or $0.52 per share, a year earlier.
The company's combined ratio was 99.8 percent for the first quarter, up from 98.2 percent for the first quarter of 1996.
